items.title: Patera
items.text:
Patera is a modular, async-first ASGI web framework for Python with a structure inspired by Java frameworks: class-based controllers, decorators for routing and HTTP semantics, dependency injection of application services, and typed configuration objects.

from pydantic import BaseModel

from patera import HttpStatus, MediaType, Request, Response
from patera.controller import Controller, consumes, get, path, post, produces

from app import App


class Greeting(BaseModel):
    name: str


@path("/api/v1/greetings")
class GreetingApi(Controller[App]):
    @get("/")
    async def hello(self, req: Request) -> Response:
        return req.res.json({"message": "Hello, World!"})

    @post("/")
    @consumes(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
    @produces(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON, HttpStatus.CREATED)
    async def greet(self, req: Request, greeting: Greeting) -> Response:
        return req.res.json({"message": f"Hello, {greeting.name}!"})

Beta

Patera is in beta. Until version 1.0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; each one is listed in the changelog. The AI interface and the desktop packages are experimental.

items.title: What is included
items.text:
The core package (patera) handles:

  • routing with class-based controllers and Werkzeug converters,
  • requests and responses with Pydantic validation and response shaping,
  • dependency injection of singleton services,
  • typed configuration from classes and environment variables,
  • templates, static files and static pages,
  • CORS, middleware and exception handlers,
  • generated OpenAPI documentation with Swagger UI,
  • logging with Loguru and JSON Lines log files,
  • a command line interface and a test client.

Optional extension packages add SQL databases, migrations, authentication, caching, scheduled tasks, e-mail, declarative API clients, JoltUI server components, an admin dashboard, an AI interface and desktop applications.

items.text:

  • Guide

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python 3.13 or newer
  • Any ASGI server; patera dev uses Uvicorn and patera prod uses Granian

items.title: The production server
items.text:
uv add "patera[prod]"
uv run patera prod --env-file .env.prod

patera prod runs Granian with DEBUG forced off.

  • Only an environment file named with --env-file is loaded; values in the process environment win.
  • The address comes from PATERA_HOST / PATERA_PORT, then the defaults on your config class, then 0.0.0.0:80. localhost is mapped to 0.0.0.0.
  • PATERA_LOOP selects the event loop.
  • The application is found in the conventional app package; select another with --app module:Class or PATERA_IMPORT.

Any other ASGI server works with the application factory:

uvicorn app:App --factory --lifespan on

items.title: Checklist
items.text:
• Keep the ASGI lifespan enabled. Database connections, caches, schedulers and cleanup hooks depend on it.
  • Set DEBUG=False (patera prod does this). Unhandled errors then become a neutral 500 and are logged.
  • Apply reviewed migrations as an explicit deployment step.
  • Restrict CORS with an explicit CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS list, especially with credentials.
  • Keep secrets in the environment, not in the configuration class or the repository.
  • Persist data outside replaceable images: databases, uploads and the log files you need. Never put private uploads under the public static directory.
  • Match the proxy's path handling to URL_PREFIX and STATIC_URL. Static files can be served by the reverse proxy directly.
  • Add a health endpoint that checks the readiness you depend on.
  • Pin dependencies and test the production configuration.

items.title: Several workers
items.text:
Each worker process has its own singletons, in-memory caches and schedulers:

  • the in-memory cache backend is not shared; use Redis or SQLite for a shared cache,
  • scheduled jobs run in every worker that starts a scheduler; choose one scheduler owner or add distributed coordination (job IDs do not prevent execution in several processes),
  • log file rotation is not coordinated between processes: set ROTATION=None and rotate externally, or run a single worker,
  • the admin dashboard request statistics are per worker.

items.title: Containers
items.text:
Docker Compose and similar tools are optional; follow your project's deployment system. A minimal image installs the project with uv and runs patera prod:

FROM python:3.13-slim
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
WORKDIR /srv/app
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev --no-install-project
COPY . .
RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev
ENV PATERA_HOST=0.0.0.0 PATERA_PORT=8000
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "patera", "prod"]

Provide the environment (database URL, secret key, ...) at runtime, and mount volumes for persistent data.

items.title: Desktop programs
items.text: To ship the application as a desktop program instead of a server, see Desktop applications.

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Optional features ship as separate packages that install into the patera namespace. Each one is a service: you subclass it, configure it through a config field named after your subclass, and register it in App.app_extensions (or inject it).

@app(__name__, configs=Config)
class App(Patera[Config]):
    app_extensions = [Databases, PublicCache, Jobs]

items.title: Admin dashboard
items.text:
patera-admin provides a web dashboard for request statistics, logs, database models, files in the static folder, task managers and e-mail clients.

uv add "patera[admin]"

items.title: Setup
items.text:
The dashboard requires an authentication middleware.

from patera.admin import AdminConfig, AdminInterface


class Admin(AdminInterface):
    MANAGED_MODELS = [Note]


class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    ADMIN: AdminConfig = AdminConfig(
        URL_FOR_FOR_LOGIN="AuthApi.login", URL_FOR_FOR_LOGOUT="AuthApi.logout",
    )

Register Admin in app_extensions. The dashboard is served at /admin/<lang>/ (en, de, sl, es), for example /admin/en/dashboard, plus URL_PREFIX when configured.

Admin looks up the extensions it manages (databases, task managers, e-mail clients) on every page load, so their order in app_extensions does not matter.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Option Default Description ADMIN_BASE_URL "/admin" Base URL of the dashboard. DEFAULT_LANGUAGE "en" en, de, sl or es. URL_FOR_FOR_LOGIN required Endpoint name of your login route (the repeated FOR is intentional). URL_FOR_FOR_LOGOUT required Endpoint name of your logout route. LOGIN_MEDIA_TYPE application/json Media type of the login response. LOGO_URL None Logo shown in the dashboard. SHOW_REMEMBER_ME False Show a "remember me" option at login. SHOW_FORGOT_PASSWORD False Show a "forgot password" option at login. REQUEST_STATISTICS True Count requests in memory and show statistics.

Admin does not create accounts or provide an authentication policy: login and logout are routes your application implements.

items.title: Permissions
items.text:
Users need roles from patera.admin.Permissions, returned by your authentication roles_loader:

Permission Allows ADMIN_CAN_ENTER opening the dashboard ADMIN_CAN_VIEW viewing records, logs and files ADMIN_CAN_CREATE creating records ADMIN_CAN_EDIT editing records ADMIN_CAN_DELETE deleting records

Each action needs ADMIN_CAN_ENTER together with its own permission. A user with ENTER and VIEW can look around but not change anything. A role named admin does not automatically grant these permissions.

items.title: Request statistics
items.text:
The dashboard opens with the application's request statistics for the last 15 minutes, hour, 6 hours or 24 hours: uptime, requests per second by status class, 2xx/4xx/5xx counts, average and 95th-percentile response times, the busiest endpoints and the most frequent error statuses. Admin counts requests in memory, so each worker process shows its own requests since it started. Set REQUEST_STATISTICS=False to turn this off.

The log view reads the application's JSON Lines log files.

items.title: Model forms
items.text:
Form metadata derives from the model's Meta (patera.database.sql.declarative_base.ModelMeta).

  • Record forms are validated with Meta.create_validation_schema / update_validation_schema when the model has them.
  • Otherwise values are converted to the column types (an unticked checkbox is False, an empty optional field None), and only fields the form shows are written: fields in exclude_from_create_form / exclude_from_update_form cannot be set through a request.
  • The admin_create, admin_update and admin_delete hooks implement application rules; raise AdminFormError from patera.admin.form_values for field errors.
  • Custom form elements in patera.admin.custom_elements (for Meta.custom_form_fields) include FileInput (the hooks receive an UploadedFile), DateInput (date or date-and-time, with optional UTC conversion) and LatexInput (text with live LaTeX math preview).

Warning

Generic CRUD does not know password hashing, ownership or publication rules. Exclude sensitive fields, provide validation schemas, and test direct requests with forged fields and insufficient permissions, not only the displayed form.

items.title: AI interface
items.text:
Experimental

This package is not yet ready for production use; its API may change in any release.

patera-aiinterface connects to chat completion APIs (OpenAI-compatible and Ollama), with prompts, chat history and retrieval augmentation.

uv add "patera[aiinterface]"
pip install "patera-aiinterface[augmentation]"   # retrieval: sentence-transformers, PyTorch, pgvector

Retrieval augmentation needs the augmentation extra; everything else works without it.

items.title: A service
items.text:
from typing import AsyncIterator, Optional

from patera.aiinterface import (
    AiService, AiServiceConfig, ChatResponse, SqlHistoryProvider, history, system_prompt, user_prompt,
)
from patera.aiinterface.service_provider.openai import OpenAIServiceProvider


class ChatHistory(SqlHistoryProvider[ChatMessageRow]):   # a model with session_id, role,
    model = ChatMessageRow                               # content and order_number columns


class Assistant(AiService):
    service_provider = OpenAIServiceProvider()           # or OllamaServiceProvider()
    history_provider = ChatHistory()

    @system_prompt("You are a helpful translator.")
    @user_prompt("Translate '<:text>' to <:language>.")
    async def translate(self, text: str, language: str = "German") -> ChatResponse: ...

    @history
    @system_prompt("You are a friendly assistant.")
    @user_prompt("<:message>")
    async def chat(self, session_id: Optional[str], message: str) -> AsyncIterator[ChatResponse]: ...


class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    ASSISTANT: AiServiceConfig = AiServiceConfig(
        BASE_URL="https://api.openai.com/v1", API_KEY="...", MODEL="gpt-4o-mini", HISTORY_LIMIT=10,
    )

answer = await self.assistant.translate("Good morning", "French")
async for chunk in self.assistant.chat(None, "Hi!"):      # None starts a new session
    session_id = chunk.session_id                         # send it back to continue the chat

Every call builds the messages the same way: the current system prompt first, then (with @history) the session's last HISTORY_LIMIT messages, then the user prompt with its <:name> placeholders filled from the method's arguments. A method annotated -> AsyncIterator[ChatResponse] streams and is iterated directly, without await; the others return one ChatResponse.

items.title: History
items.text:
@history needs a history_provider and a session_id parameter on the method.

  • None starts a new session (a random UUID by default; override new_session_id()), and every response carries the session id.
  • The question and the answer are saved after the call (a streamed answer once the stream ends); nothing is saved when the call fails.
  • The system prompt is never stored, so a changed prompt applies to existing sessions too.
  • In a @transactional handler, SqlHistoryProvider uses the request's session, so the messages commit or roll back with the request. Anywhere else it uses a short transaction of its own, so it works in plain requests, CLI commands and scheduled jobs.
  • Writes to one chat session never overlap, also across worker processes: each write first locks the chat session until it commits (an advisory lock on PostgreSQL, the database's write lock on SQLite). Other databases take turns within a process.
  • Implement load() and append() of BaseHistoryProvider for other storage.

Enforce ownership of conversation and session identifiers in your application.

items.title: Summaries
items.text: HISTORY_SUMMARY = HistorySummaryConfig(EVERY=10, MAX_WORDS=250) keeps a rolling summary of long conversations. Each call sends the summary, then the messages it does not cover. Once EVERY messages beyond the latest HISTORY_LIMIT are uncovered, they are merged into the summary by one extra model call in the background, after the answer is returned. The summary is a row of the messages table (role="summary"), every message stays stored in full, and concurrent updates never overwrite each other. await service.update_summary(session_id) runs an update by hand. Custom history providers support it by implementing load_since, load_summary and save_summary.

items.title: Retrieval augmentation
items.text:
@augmentation adds the most similar documents as a context message just before the user message (CONTEXT_TEMPLATE, with <:documents>); the history never stores them. With history and REWRITE_QUERY=True, a follow-up such as "who wrote it?" is first rewritten by the model into a standalone question for the search (one extra call per message; off by default).

The documents are rows with a text and a VectorColumn (pgvector's type):

from patera.aiinterface.augmentation_provider import BaseAugmentationProvider
from patera.aiinterface.augmentation_provider.embeddings import VectorColumn


class Document(Base):
    __tablename__ = "documents"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    text: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text)
    vector = mapped_column(VectorColumn(384))     # the embedding model's dimension


class Documents(BaseAugmentationProvider[Document]):
    model = Document

    def base_query(self, req):                    # optional: limit the candidates
        return select(Document).where(Document.owner_id == req.user.id)


class Assistant(AiService):
    ...
    augmentation_provider = Documents()
  • The embedding model is loaded the first time a text is embedded (in a worker thread), not when the application starts, so CLI commands never load it. Override load_embedding_model() to use another model.
  • await assistant.augmentation_provider.add_documents(texts, **columns) embeds and stores documents with the same model that embeds the questions.
  • On PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension the search is one query ordered by cosine distance; on other databases the candidates are compared in Python (RETRIEVAL forces either).
  • Settings: AiServiceConfig.AUGMENTATION = AugmentationConfig(MATCH_LIMIT=5, MINIMAL_SIMILARITY=0.9, ...).

A missing provider for @history or @augmentation fails when the service starts.

items.title: Other settings
items.text:
RESPONSE_FORMAT (for example {"type": "json_object"}), TEMPERATURE (None for the provider's default), MAX_RETRIES (failed connections), ORGANIZATION_ID and PROJECT_ID (OpenAI headers).

Safety

Use fake providers in tests. Keep untrusted retrieved text separate from application instructions, bound history and retrieval work, handle provider errors and stream cancellation, and never let generated text authorize application actions.

A complete example lives in examples/ai_chat.

items.title: External APIs
items.text:
patera-apiinterface turns annotated methods into HTTP calls with HTTPX: declarative async clients for external APIs.

uv add "patera[apiinterface]"

from patera import HttpMethod
from patera.apiinterface import ApiInterface, AuthType, auth, headers, method, resource, service, timeout


@service("GITHUB_URL")                         # config key or literal URL
@auth(AuthType.BEARER, token="GITHUB_TOKEN")   # config key or literal value
@headers({"X-Client": "my-app"})
@timeout(10)
class GithubApi(ApiInterface):

    @method(HttpMethod.GET)
    @resource("/repos/<repo_id>")              # filled from the argument of the same name
    async def get_repo(self, repo_id: int) -> Repo: ...   # Pydantic return types are validated

    @method(HttpMethod.POST)
    @resource("/repos")
    async def create_repo(self, name: str, private: bool) -> dict: ...   # arguments become the JSON body

Declare GITHUB_URL and GITHUB_TOKEN on your config and inject the interface. Decorated method bodies are replaced by wrappers, so put business logic in a separate service.

items.title: Arguments
items.text:
• Arguments fill <name> placeholders in the resource (encoded).
  • The remaining arguments become query parameters for GET and HEAD, and the body otherwise.
  • @consumes / @produces select the body and response formats, including form data and file uploads. These are the API interface's decorators, not the controller decorators of the same name.

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
@auth supports AuthType.BEARER, AuthType.BASIC_AUTH and AuthType.API_KEY. Class-level defaults can be overridden on methods; @no_auth disables inherited authentication for one method.

@forward_request (on a method or the class) additionally forwards the current request's query string and fills placeholders from its route parameters. Forwarding is explicit, so incoming credentials and query values are not passed on by accident.

items.title: Responses and errors
items.text:
• A Pydantic return annotation validates the remote data.
  • A 4xx or 5xx answer raises ApiInterfaceResponseError with status_code, the decoded body and the response.
  • Annotate a method with -> httpx.Response to receive every response unchecked; the caller must then inspect it.

items.title: Client lifecycle
items.text:
• Within an application lifespan, an interface reuses one HTTP client and closes it at shutdown.
  • Standalone and CLI calls use temporary clients, closed before the call returns, including on failures.
  • If you acquire interface.client explicitly, call await interface.aclose() in that same event loop before it closes. Access from another loop raises instead of discarding an unclosed client.
  • Override create_client() for transport mocks or limits. Test with an HTTPX mock transport, including error and timeout behaviour.

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
patera-auth provides an authentication and authorization middleware, with helpers for cookies, JWT, roles and password hashing.

uv add "patera[auth]"

items.title: The authentication middleware
items.text:
Subclass Authentication and implement how users and roles are loaded:

# app/middleware/auth_mw.py
import jwt

from patera import Request
from patera.auth import Authentication, AuthUtils
from patera.middleware import middleware


@middleware
class TokenAuth(Authentication):
    async def user_loader(self, req: Request):
        token = req.headers.get("authorization", "").removeprefix("Bearer ")
        try:
            claims = AuthUtils.validate_jwt_token(token, self.app.configs.SECRET_KEY)
        except jwt.InvalidTokenError:
            return None                    # -> not authenticated
        return await load_user(claims["sub"])

    async def roles_loader(self, user) -> list:
        return user.roles
  • user_loader(req) returns the account or None; roles_loader(user) returns its role list.
  • Mark the class with @middleware without an order: Authentication uses -99, inside the database session boundary, so loaders can use the database.
  • Inject an account service for credential lookup.

items.title: Protecting routes
items.text:
from patera.auth import login_required, role_required


@path("/account")
@login_required()                       # every endpoint requires a user
class AccountApi(Controller[App]):

    @get("/")
    async def me(self, req: Request) -> Response:
        return req.res.json({"user": req.user.name})

    @get("/admin")
    @role_required("admin", "owner")    # any of the listed roles
    async def admin(self, req: Request) -> Response: ...

    @get("/audit")
    @role_required("admin", "auditor", require_all=True)    # every listed role
    async def audit(self, req: Request) -> Response: ...
  • A missing user raises AuthenticationException (401); missing roles raise AuthorizationException (403, the required roles in data). Both produce JSON error responses unless you handle them.
  • @role_required implies authentication. Role requirements on the controller and on the endpoint must both be satisfied.
  • Routes without the decorators do not load the user, even when cookies exist, and ALWAYS_LOAD_ROLES does not change that. Pages with optional login must load the account explicitly.
  • The decorators do not protect WebSockets or static files.
  • Check object ownership in your services as well.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The configuration model is AuthConfig, read from the field named after your subclass:

from patera.auth import AuthConfig

class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    TOKEN_AUTH: AuthConfig = AuthConfig(
        AUTHENTICATION_ERROR_MSG="Please sign in",
        AUTHORIZATION_ERROR_MSG="Not allowed",
        ALWAYS_LOAD_ROLES=False,
    )

Override refresh_credentials(res) to renew cookies or tokens on responses.

items.title: AuthUtils
items.text:
Helper Description create_password_hash / check_password_hash bcrypt over a SHA-256 digest, so passwords of any length count in full; a malformed stored hash simply does not match; plain bcrypt hashes from earlier versions still verify password_hash_needs_update(hash) says when to re-hash after a successful login create_signed_cookie_value / decode_signed_cookie(value, key, max_age=None) HMAC with a signing timestamp; max_age rejects older values create_jwt_token / validate_jwt_token HS256; validation raises jwt.InvalidTokenError

The password helpers are synchronous and deliberately slow; offload them with asyncio.to_thread in async handlers.

Sessions and CSRF

Signed cookies detect tampering; they do not provide secrecy or revocation. For browser sessions choose cookie Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite deliberately, enforce CSRF protection on state-changing requests, and implement expiry and revocation. Patera's authentication metadata does not supply the application's whole session and CSRF policy. Catch expected credential failures, not every exception: a database outage is not bad credentials.

items.title: Caching
items.text:
patera-caching caches endpoint responses with in-memory, Redis and SQLite backends.

uv add "patera[caching]"            # in-memory backend
uv add "patera[caching-redis]"      # + Redis backend
uv add "patera[caching-sqlite]"     # + SQLite backend

items.title: Setup
items.text:
from patera.caching import Caching, CachingConfig, cache


class PublicCache(Caching):
    pass                                 # in-memory backend by default


class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    PUBLIC_CACHE: CachingConfig = CachingConfig(DURATION=60, MAX_SIZE=1000)


@path("/stats")
class StatsApi(Controller[App]):
    @get("/")
    @cache("PUBLIC_CACHE", duration=15)  # registered name of the extension
    async def stats(self, req: Request) -> Response:
        return req.res.json(await compute_stats())

Register PublicCache in app_extensions. Put @cache directly above the handler (below @get).

The default in-memory backend is per instance, bounded in size and with expiry. It is neither shared across worker processes nor persistent across restarts.

items.title: What is cached
items.text:
• Only GET and HEAD are cached by default. Opt into POST explicitly for read-only RPC operations with @cache("PUBLIC_CACHE", methods=("POST",)); cache hits skip the handler, and opted-in methods include a SHA-256 body digest in the key.
  • Only successful (< 400), non-streaming responses without cookies are cached; file sends are skipped too.
  • The body is stored as it is sent, already serialized (through Response[Model]), and replayed with the status, headers and media type on a hit.

items.title: Keys
items.text:
The default key combines the handler's module and qualified name, the method, the path and the ordered query string, plus a user identity suffix when a user is loaded.

key accepts a string or a sync/async callable taking the Request:

@cache("PUBLIC_CACHE", key=lambda req: f"page:{req.path}:{req.headers.get('accept-language', '')}")

A custom key replaces the default URL/handler key, so include every relevant variation. Body digests and user partitioning still apply.

Cache only public data

Use per_user=False only for genuinely shared results. Per-user separation needs a loaded user with a stable identity, and public routes normally skip user loading. Tenant, language or permission variants may need custom keys.

items.title: Manual use
items.text:
await cache.get(key, req)
await cache.set(key, response, duration)
await cache.delete(key)
await cache.delete("users:*", wildcard=True)
await cache.delete(r"^users:\d+$", regex=True)
await cache.clear()

Invalidate on writes with delete/clear or by using revisioned keys.

items.title: Backends
items.text:
Other backends are chosen with backend_class; the extension creates them from its settings with backend_class.from_configs(app, configs, namespace):

from patera.caching.backends.redis_cache_backend import RedisCacheBackend


class SharedCache(Caching):
    backend_class = RedisCacheBackend   # SHARED_CACHE = {"REDIS_URL": ..., "DURATION": 60}
  • Keys in Redis and SQLite live under KEY_PREFIX, by default patera:<app name>:<cache name>: (for example patera:blog:shared_cache:), so several caches or applications can share one store, and clear() only removes its own keys.
  • The Redis and SQLite backends store JSON (the serialized body as base64 text), so reading an entry never runs code; an entry that cannot be read counts as a miss.
  • To build a backend yourself, assign self.backend in init() before calling super().init().
  • Custom backends implement patera.caching.BaseCacheBackend (encode_payload() / decode_payload() convert a payload).

items.title: SQL databases
items.text:
patera-database integrates async SQLAlchemy: databases, request sessions, repositories and transactions.

uv add "patera[database]"

Install a driver for your database too: aiosqlite is included; use for example asyncpg for PostgreSQL.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
# app/database.py
from sqlalchemy import Integer, String
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from patera.database.sql import DeclarativeBaseModel, SqlDatabase, SqlDatabaseManager


class MainDb(SqlDatabase):
    __db_name__ = "main"


class Databases(SqlDatabaseManager):
    databases = [MainDb]


class Base(DeclarativeBaseModel):
    __abstract__ = True
    __db_name__ = "main"          # models are bound to a database by name


class Note(Base):
    __tablename__ = "notes"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))

# app/configs.py
from patera.database.sql import SqlDatabaseConfig

class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    MAIN_DB: SqlDatabaseConfig = SqlDatabaseConfig(DATABASE_URI="sqlite+aiosqlite:///./app.db")

# app/__init__.py
@app(__name__, configs=Config)
class App(Patera[Config]):
    app_extensions = [Databases]

The engine connects on startup and is disposed on shutdown. Register only the manager, not the individual databases; injecting a database independently first can bypass the manager setup.

Distinguish the class and its config key (MainDb / MAIN_DB), the database name (main) and the session name. With several databases, give each one a unique __db_name__ and a unique DATABASE_SESSION_NAME.

Schemas

Declaring models does not create or migrate tables. Use migrations for schema evolution; metadata.create_all is only for disposable or brand-new schemas.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
SqlDatabaseConfig:

Option Default Description DATABASE_URI required SQLAlchemy async URL. DATABASE_SESSION_NAME "session" Name of the request session; unique per database. SHOW_SQL False Log every executed SQL statement. NICE_NAME None Display name in the admin dashboard; defaults to the database name. EXPIRE_ON_COMMIT False Expire session objects on commit. AUTOFLUSH False Autoflush the session. SQLITE_FOREIGN_KEYS False SQLite only: run PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every connection so FOREIGN KEY constraints (such as ON DELETE CASCADE) are enforced. SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT None SQLite only: seconds a connection waits for another connection's lock before failing with "database is locked". None keeps the driver's default of 5 seconds, or a ?timeout= in DATABASE_URI. 
PATERA_MAIN_DB__DATABASE_URI=postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@db/app
PATERA_MAIN_DB__SQLITE_FOREIGN_KEYS=true

items.title: Sessions and transactions
items.text:
During a request, model queries and repositories share one session per database. At the end of the request, the manager middleware commits it if the controller or endpoint is marked @transactional and no exception occurred; otherwise all changes are rolled back.

from patera.database.sql import Repository, query, transactional
from patera.injectable import Inject


class NoteRepository(Repository[Note]):
    model = Note

    @query("SELECT * FROM notes WHERE title LIKE :pattern ORDER BY id")
    async def search(self, pattern: str) -> list[Note]: ...   # SQL with bound parameters


@path("/notes")
class NoteApi(Controller[App]):
    notes: Inject[NoteRepository]

    @get("/")
    async def index(self, req: Request) -> Response:
        page = await Note.query().order_by(Note.id).paginate(page=1, per_page=20)
        return req.res.json({"total": page.total, "titles": [n.title for n in page.items]})

    @post("/")
    @transactional
    async def create(self, req: Request) -> Response:
        note = await self.notes.create_and_flush(title=(await req.json())["title"])
        return req.res.json({"id": note.id}).status(201)
  • Successful body conversion happens before the commit. A failure after the commit (for example while streaming) cannot undo it.
  • Do not close the request session manually or reuse it in background work.

items.title: Queries
items.text:
Model.query() returns a chainable AsyncQuery:

  • builders: where / filter, filter_by, join, order_by, order_by_strings("title DESC"), limit, offset,
  • terminal methods: all, first, one, one_or_none, count, exists, paginate.

items.title: Repositories
items.text:
Repository[Model] subclasses set model = Model and offer get, get_one_by, first_by, list_all, list_by, count, exists, create, create_and_flush, add, add_all, save, delete, flush, refresh, paginate and execute.

@query methods run SQL with bound parameters and map rows to models, Pydantic or dataclass types, dicts or scalars based on the return annotation (Optional[...] allows no result).

Repositories are shared singletons; they use the context-bound session and do not own a session.

items.title: Outside requests
items.text:
Outside HTTP requests, open sessions explicitly:

async with db.create_session() as session:
    notes = await Note.query(session).all()
Tool Use db.create_session() a plain session; manage transactions yourself async with db.session_scope() a context-bound session that commits on success and rolls back on exceptions @cli_session("main") opens a session and a transaction for a CLI command @background_session("main") a managed session for a scheduled job (place it below @schedule_job)

Give each database its own scope.

items.title: The manager
items.text: SqlDatabaseManager gives access to the databases: manager.get_database("main"), manager["main"], manager.get_default_database().

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Application startup hooks run before the extension's connection hooks; a schema action in an early hook must connect explicitly first.
  • Keep SQLite write transactions short; timeout settings do not make SQLite a multi-writer database.
  • Socket handlers: see WebSockets.

items.title: Desktop applications
items.text:
Experimental

This package is not yet ready for production use; its API may change in any release.

patera-desktop shows a Patera application in a native window (pywebview) and packages it as a program with PyInstaller.

uv add "patera[desktop]"
uv add "patera-desktop[pyinstaller]"   # to package the application

For Python-authored browser pages and components, add Desktop UI. Applications using ordinary HTML and JavaScript do not need it.

items.title: Running in a window
items.text:
Register the extension; it adds the desktop:* CLI commands:

from patera.desktop import Desktop


@app(__name__, configs=Config)
class App(Patera[Config]):
    app_extensions = [Desktop]

uv run patera cli desktop:run        # the development server, with auto-reload
uv run patera cli desktop:run prod   # the production server

The command starts the application in a separate process, as patera dev or patera prod would, on 127.0.0.1 and the application's PORT setting. Once it answers, a window titled with APP_NAME (or DESKTOP.TITLE) opens the index page. Closing the window stops the application.

items.title: Window settings
items.text:
from patera.desktop import DesktopConfig


class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    DESKTOP: DesktopConfig = DesktopConfig(
        INDEX_PAGE="/dashboard",
        WIDTH=1200,
        HEIGHT=800,
        BACKGROUND_COLOR="#17191C",
    )
Setting Default Meaning INDEX_PAGE "/" The page the window opens: a path relative to URL_PREFIX, or an absolute URL. TITLE APP_NAME The window's title. WIDTH, HEIGHT 1024 × 720 The window's size at the first start. MIN_WIDTH, MIN_HEIGHT 480 × 360 The smallest the user can make it. REMEMBER_GEOMETRY True Reopen the window with the size, position and maximized state it had when it was closed. A window whose screen is gone opens centered. MAXIMIZED, FULLSCREEN False Open maximized, or in full screen (which is not remembered). RESIZABLE, ON_TOP True, False CONFIRM_CLOSE False Ask before the window closes. BACKGROUND_COLOR "#FFFFFF" Shown before the page has loaded; match the page to avoid a flash. TEXT_SELECT True The user can select and copy the page's text. ZOOMABLE False The user can zoom with Ctrl and ±. PERSIST_STORAGE True Keep cookies and local storage between starts (so a signed-in user stays signed in). Off: they are forgotten when the window closes. ICON None Icon file relative to the application's folder (.ico on Windows, .icns on macOS, .png on Linux). Linux shows it on the window; Windows and macOS show the executable's icon, which desktop:spec takes from this setting. DEV_TOOLS None The web inspector, from the page's context menu ("Inspect"). Not set: on for desktop:run in dev mode and when DEBUG is on. GUI None pywebview's toolkit, for example "qt" or "gtk" on Linux.

The window's last size and position (window.json) and the web view's storage (webview/) are kept in the user's data folder (see below), not in pywebview's shared folder.

items.title: Packaging a program
items.text:
uv run patera cli desktop:package                  # into dist/desktop
uv run patera cli desktop:package installer/files  # into another folder

The result is a folder, dist/desktop/<APP_NAME>/, with the executable and everything it needs; ship the whole folder (an installer such as Inno Setup can wrap it). PyInstaller builds for the system it runs on, so build the Windows program on Windows.

The packaged program runs the server in a background thread inside its own process, on 127.0.0.1, in production mode, through run_in_window(App), and closes it with the window. It listens on the port of its last start when that is free, otherwise on a free one, which it keeps for the next start: browsers keep local storage per origin, port included.

items.title: The spec file
items.text:
PyInstaller builds from a spec file. When the application needs more than the defaults, write one and edit it:

uv run patera cli desktop:spec                     # writes desktop.spec
uv run patera cli desktop:spec specs/windows.spec  # or another file

desktop:package builds with desktop.spec when the project has one (another file: desktop:package dist/desktop specs/windows.spec), otherwise with a generated one in build/desktop/. pyinstaller desktop.spec works too. desktop:spec does not overwrite an existing file; delete it to start again.

Setting Default What it is for PACKAGE_EXCLUDES runtime files Files and folders of the application package that are not copied (see below). HIDDEN_IMPORTS [] Modules PyInstaller does not find, such as ones imported by name (plugins, importlib). COLLECT_SUBMODULES the app package, uvicorn Packages included with every module they have. COLLECT_DATA patera and the extensions used Packages whose data files (templates, static files) are included. DATAS, BINARIES [] More files, folders and DLLs: (source, folder in the program). EXCLUDES mypy, pytest Modules left out. ICON None The program's icon (.ico on Windows, .icns on macOS). CONSOLE False Show a console window with the program's output, handy when debugging. ONE_FILE False One executable file instead of a folder. It is unpacked at every start, so it starts slower. ENTRY_SCRIPT None Your own entry script instead of the generated one.

Paths are relative to the spec file. Below the settings is ordinary PyInstaller code (Analysis, EXE, COLLECT), which you can change as well.

The generated entry script is three lines; write your own (and set ENTRY_SCRIPT) if you need to prepare something first:

from app import App
from patera.desktop import run_in_window

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_in_window(App)

items.title: The program's settings
items.text:
A packaged program reads no .env: that file holds development values and often secrets. Its settings come from desktop.env, a file in the project that is bundled into the program:

uv run patera cli desktop:env      # writes desktop.env from the configuration class

The file lists every setting the configuration class declares (not the built-in ones), with its default in a commented line; remove the # to change one. A required setting is an empty line, and desktop:package refuses to build until it has a value. Values are never copied from .env. ${PATERA_DATA_DIR} is the user's data folder:

PATERA_MAIN_DB__DATABASE_URI=sqlite+aiosqlite:///${PATERA_DATA_DIR}/app.db
PATERA_DESKTOP__WIDTH=1200

At every start the program loads, each over the next: environment variables, the installation's settings.env in the data folder (settings_file(APP_NAME)), desktop.env, and the configuration class's defaults. desktop:run loads desktop.env too, under the development .env. APP_NAME names the data folder, so it comes from the class, desktop.env or the environment, not from settings.env.

Secrets

Anyone with a copy of the program can read desktop.env, so it holds no passwords, keys or tokens; desktop:package warns about values whose names look like secrets. When the configuration declares SECRET_KEY, the program makes a key of its own at its first start and keeps it in the installation's settings.env, unless a variable sets one.

items.title: Things to keep in mind
items.text:
• The application must be in a package (app/__init__.py). The package folder is copied next to the executable, because Patera finds controllers, exception handlers, middleware and templates through its files. What running and developing leave in it is skipped: __pycache__, logs and the folder of LOG_FILES.PATH, *.log, SQLite databases and their journals, .env files and tool caches. Change PACKAGE_EXCLUDES for more, or remove "*.db" to ship a database.
  • What differs per user or installation goes into settings_file(APP_NAME). The application may write it, for example from a settings page; changes apply at the next start.
  • The program's own folder may not be writable (Program Files) and is replaced by every update. Keep data in user_data_dir(APP_NAME) (%APPDATA%\<name> on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/<name> on macOS, ~/.local/share/<name> on Linux), with ${PATERA_DATA_DIR} in desktop.env or user_data_dir(APP_NAME) in code. The packaged program writes its log files there by default.

A complete notes program with a database, a page and a spec file lives in examples/desktop_notes.

items.title: E-mail
items.text:
patera-email is an async SMTP e-mail client with Jinja templates.

uv add "patera[email]"

items.title: Setup
items.text:
from patera.email import EmailClient, EmailConfig


class Mailer(EmailClient):
    pass


class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    MAILER: EmailConfig = EmailConfig(
        SENDER_NAME_OR_ADDRESS="My app <noreply@example.com>",
        SMTP_SERVER="smtp.example.com", SMTP_PORT=587,
        USERNAME="user", PASSWORD="secret", USE_TLS=True,
    )

Register Mailer in app_extensions or inject it. Keep credentials in environment-backed settings, for example PATERA_MAILER__PASSWORD.

items.title: Sending
items.text:
mailer: Inject[Mailer]
...
await self.mailer.send_email(
    "ana@example.com", "Report", "See attachment", attachments={"report.csv": data},
)
await self.mailer.send_email_with_template(
    ["a@example.com"], "Welcome", "mail/welcome.txt", context={"name": "Ana"},
)
  • The recipient is one address string or a list; a comma-separated string is not split.
  • Attachments map file names to bytes.
  • Each send opens its own SMTP connection.

items.title: TLS
items.text:
• USE_TLS means STARTTLS (commonly port 587).
  • USE_SSL means implicit TLS (commonly port 465).
  • They are mutually exclusive. Credentials are used only when both username and password are set.

items.title: Reliability
items.text: A send is an external side effect that a database rollback cannot undo. When delivery must track committed business operations, use a durable outbox and an idempotent retry strategy; an in-memory background task alone does not guarantee delivery after a crash. In tests, use a capture service or a fake client.

items.title: JoltUI
items.text:
patera-joltui serves server components for JoltUI, the TypeScript SPA framework by Marko Šterk, with typed group registration.

uv add "patera[joltui]"

items.title: Setup
items.text:
from html import escape

from patera import Request
from patera.injectable import Inject
from patera.joltui import (
    ComponentGroup, JoltuiGroupHandler, PateraJoltui,
    component, group, joltui_request,
)


@group("default")
class DefaultGroupHandler(JoltuiGroupHandler):
    @component("home-page")
    async def home_page(self, req: Request):
        return req.res.html_body("<h1>Welcome</h1>")


@group("user-group")
class UserGroupHandler(JoltuiGroupHandler):
    @component("user-page")
    async def user_page(self, req: Request):
        data = joltui_request(req)
        user_id = escape(str(data.route_parameters["user_id"]))
        return req.res.html_body(f"<h1>User {user_id}</h1>")


class JoltuiInterface(PateraJoltui):
    default_group: ComponentGroup[DefaultGroupHandler]
    user_group: ComponentGroup[UserGroupHandler]

Register JoltuiInterface in app_extensions, or inject it with joltui: Inject[JoltuiInterface]. The extension registers its own controller; no application controller or manual dispatch route is needed.

Set JoltUI's serverComponentsUrl to /joltui/components (including Patera's URL_PREFIX, if configured). Change the endpoint with JoltuiConfig.COMPONENTS_PATH:

JOLTUI_INTERFACE = {"COMPONENTS_PATH": "/components"}

items.title: The request envelope
items.text:
JoltUI sends a JSON POST containing tagName, groupName, routeParameters, queryParameters and attributes.

  • Omitted or null groups default to default; omitted or null parameter mappings default to empty dictionaries.
  • Tags are trimmed and lowercased; group names remain case-sensitive.
  • Malformed requests return 400; unknown groups or components return 404.

Handlers receive the original Patera Request, with cookies, sessions, headers, request context and response helpers. joltui_request(req) provides the validated frontend metadata as tag_name, group_name, route_parameters, query_parameters and attributes. HTTP URL parameters stay unchanged, and the original JSON is available through await req.json().

items.title: Responses
items.text:
Always return a Patera Response with content type text/html, for example req.res.html_body(markup) or await req.res.html("user.html", ...). Plain strings and non-HTML successful responses are rejected. Sync handlers are supported.

Error responses (status 400 or higher), including the JSON 415 of @consumes and lifecycle-generated errors, keep their normal media type and status. Handler exceptions follow Patera's normal exception pipeline, including 401 and 403.

items.title: Validated bodies
items.text:
Handlers may declare an optional third argument annotated with any Pydantic model. The extension validates the full JSON body into that model; @consumes is not required. Validation failures return 422 before the handler runs (after authentication and @before_request hooks).

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from patera import Response


class UserRoute(BaseModel):
    user_id: int


class UserPageBody(BaseModel):
    route_parameters: UserRoute = Field(alias="routeParameters")
    # tagName and groupName need not be declared in a custom model.


@group("user-group")
class UserGroupHandler(JoltuiGroupHandler):
    @component("user-page")
    async def user_page(self, req: Request, body: UserPageBody) -> Response:
        return req.res.html_body(f"<h1>User {body.route_parameters.user_id}</h1>")

For the body {"tagName": "user-page", "groupName": "user-group", "routeParameters": {"user_id": "42"}}, body.route_parameters.user_id is the integer 42. Use JoltuiRequest as the third argument when its standard fields suffice (tag_name defaults to None, group_name to "default").

items.title: Groups are controllers
items.text:
Group handlers are Patera controllers. Use the normal decorators, including group and component @login_required() / @role_required(), @after_init, @before_request, @after_request, @consumes, @produces, @cors, @no_cors, @max_content_length, @ignore and @development:

from patera import MediaType
from patera.auth import login_required, role_required
from patera.controller import after_request, produces


@group("user-group")
@login_required()
class UserGroupHandler(JoltuiGroupHandler):
    @after_request
    def prevent_caching(self, res):
        res.set_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")

    @component("user-page")
    @role_required("admin")
    @produces(MediaType.TEXT_HTML)
    async def user_page(self, req: Request):
        return req.res.html_body("<h1>Users</h1>")
  • Groups are application-scoped singletons and support Inject[T]. Do not store per-request data on them.
  • Inherited component methods are exposed; overriding a method without @component removes its registration. Duplicate group names or component tags fail at initialization.
  • Only decorated methods in explicitly declared groups are callable. Interface annotations may be inherited, overridden, or removed with a non-ComponentGroup annotation.
  • Component selection runs before CORS, database, authentication and application middleware. Middleware sees the selected component as req.route_handler and its group as current_request.controller.

items.title: Caching, CORS and limits
items.text:
• Response caching defaults to GET/HEAD. To cache a read-only component, opt in with @cache("PUBLIC_CACHE", methods=("POST",)); the default key includes a digest of the complete body.
  • All components share one POST URL. They are not separate OpenAPI routes, and no WebSocket transport is provided.
  • OPTIONS preflights have no component body, so they use the shared endpoint's global CORS policy; configure it to permit the frontend. Component CORS overrides apply to actual POST responses.
  • The application's body limit protects envelope parsing; component @max_content_length limits are enforced after selection.

Warning

Frontend metadata is client input, not an authorization source. Escape values inserted into raw HTML, or use templates.

items.title: Migrations
items.text:
patera-migrate adds SQL migrations based on pyway.

uv add "patera[migrate]"

Add the Migrate mixin to the database class and keep the database manager registration:

from patera.database.sql import SqlDatabase
from patera.migrate import Migrate


class MainDb(SqlDatabase, Migrate):
    __db_name__ = "main"

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Migration settings are part of the database configuration (MAIN_DB above). The public model for these fields is MigrateConfig (from patera.migrate import MigrateConfig); the former private name _PateraPywayConfigs remains an alias.

Option Default Description MIGRATE_CLI_NAME "migrate" CLI controller name; unique per database. MIGRATE_DATABASE_MIGRATION_DIR "migrations" Folder, relative to the application package. MIGRATE_TABLE "pyway_migrations" Table that records applied migrations. MIGRATE_SQL_MIGRATION_PREFIX "V" File name prefix. MIGRATE_SQL_MIGRATION_SEPARATOR "__" Separator between version and description. MIGRATE_SQL_MIGRATION_SUFFIXES ".sql" File endings, several separated by commas.

items.title: Migration files
items.text:
A migration is named <prefix><version><separator><description><suffix>, for example V1_0__create_notes.sql. The version has at least two numbers (1_0, 2.1, 3_0_1).

  • Files with another ending, such as a README.md, are ignored.
  • A file with a migration ending but another name stops the command with an error, so a misnamed migration is never skipped silently.
  • Patera does not generate migration SQL from model differences: write and review the SQL.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
uv run patera cli migrate:init       # writes app/migrations/.pyway.conf (keep it in .gitignore)
# add migrations/V01_01__create_notes.sql
uv run patera cli migrate:info
uv run patera cli migrate:migrate
uv run patera cli migrate:validate

migrate:init writes .pyway.conf into the migration directory. Each developer generates their own copy, so add it to .gitignore. The file holds only migration settings: the connection (including the password) is read from DATABASE_URI each time a command runs. A database_* value set in the file overrides the URI for that developer.

Use patera cli --list to see the migration commands of every database.

items.title: Good practice
items.text:
• Do not rewrite applied migrations to resolve checksum mismatches; add a new migration.
  • Test both a fresh database and the upgrade path.
  • Apply reviewed migrations as an explicit deployment step. The CLI does not start the ASGI lifespan.

items.title: Task manager
items.text:
patera-taskmanager schedules jobs with APScheduler.

uv add "patera[taskmanager]"

from patera.taskmanager import TaskManager, schedule_job


class Jobs(TaskManager):

    @schedule_job("interval", minutes=5, id="cleanup")
    async def cleanup(self) -> None:
        self.app.logger.info("Cleaning up")

    @schedule_job("cron", hour=3, id="nightly")
    async def nightly(self) -> None: ...

Register Jobs in app_extensions; the scheduler starts and stops with the application lifespan (constructing the app alone does not run jobs). Decorator arguments go to APScheduler; use explicit timezones for calendar triggers.

  • A job without an id gets <class>.<method> (Jobs.cleanup).
  • A job is replaced at every start, so it is never stored twice.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
from patera.taskmanager import TaskManagerConfig

class Config(BaseConfig):
    ...
    JOBS: TaskManagerConfig = TaskManagerConfig(NICE_NAME="Jobs", DAEMON=True)

items.title: Runtime API
items.text:
Method Description add_job(func, trigger, **kwargs) add a job remove_job(job), pause_job(job), resume_job(job) manage a job run_job_now(job) run a job immediately get_job(id), jobs look up jobs is_job_running(job) state run_background_task(func, *args) fire-and-forget work

Customize the scheduler with the class attributes scheduler_cls, job_stores, executors and job_defaults.

items.title: Database access in jobs
items.text:
Jobs have no HTTP request session. Use explicit sessions or @background_session("main") from patera.database.sql, placed below @schedule_job, to give repositories a managed session:

from patera.database.sql import background_session


class Jobs(TaskManager):
    notes: Inject[NoteRepository]

    @schedule_job("interval", hours=1, id="purge")
    @background_session("main")
    async def purge(self) -> None:
        ...

items.title: Persistent job stores
items.text:
With a job store that keeps jobs outside the process, such as SQLAlchemyJobStore, declared jobs and task manager methods passed to add_job() are stored by name and find the running task manager when they run.

  • Set TaskManagerConfig(JOB_NAMESPACE="my-app-jobs"). Keep the namespace stable across restarts and unique for separate applications or stores using the same manager class.
  • An empty namespace preserves existing stored job identifiers, but only one such manager may be active per process. A duplicate fails at startup instead of redirecting jobs to another app. Registrations are removed at shutdown.
  • Separate applications need separate job store instances; do not share a store object.
  • Persistent stores serialize jobs; do not pass application-bound state as job arguments.

items.title: Several workers
items.text:
Job IDs prevent duplicate registration within one scheduler, not execution in several processes. With several workers, choose one scheduler owner or add distributed coordination, and keep jobs idempotent.

For short in-process work without scheduling, the core run_in_background() is enough; see The application class.

items.title: Desktop UI
items.text:
Experimental

This package is not yet ready for production use; its API may change in any release.

patera-desktop-ui lets you write the user interface of a desktop application in Python, using a locally bundled PyScript / Pyodide interpreter.

uv add "patera[desktop-ui]"

It requires patera-desktop>=0.11.2 for namespace and packaging integration.

The backend stays native Python. Browser controllers, components and models run in a separate interpreter and communicate with Patera HTTP endpoints. Native database sessions, files and services do not cross that boundary.

This page covers setup, pages, builds and packaging. Layouts, reactive fragments, lifecycle hooks, authorization and server-rendered components are described in the runtime guide.

items.title: Application structure
items.text:
Keep browser sources outside the backend package, so backend discovery and PyInstaller do not import browser modules:

project/
  app/__init__.py
  app/configs.py
  app/api/notes_api.py
  frontend/
    frontend/__init__.py
    templates/note.html
  ui-runtime/             complete local runtime, including runtime.json
  build/ui/               generated, do not commit

from patera import Patera, app
from patera.desktop import Desktop
from patera.desktop.ui import DesktopUI

from .configs import Config


@app(__name__, configs=Config)
class App(Patera[Config]):
    app_extensions = [Desktop, DesktopUI]

from patera import BaseConfig
from patera.desktop import DesktopConfig
from patera.desktop.ui import DesktopUIConfig


class Config(BaseConfig):
    DESKTOP: DesktopConfig = DesktopConfig(INDEX_PAGE="/app/")
    DESKTOP_UI: DesktopUIConfig = DesktopUIConfig(TITLE="Notes")

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Paths in DesktopUIConfig are relative to the backend application's root:

Setting Default Meaning SOURCE ../frontend Dedicated browser source root ENTRYPOINT frontend:app An Application instance; never imported during build RUNTIME ../ui-runtime Complete offline runtime and hash manifest OUTPUT ../build/ui Build artifacts, outside source/runtime folders MOUNT /app Shell and page URLs ASSETS /__ui__ Immutable asset URLs TITLE Patera Initial window document title PUBLIC {} Explicitly public browser configuration API_PATHS ['/api'] API prefixes requiring the UI session token

URL_PREFIX applies to the shell, assets and API prefixes. Mounts must be disjoint, non-root paths. Ordinary Patera endpoints outside these prefixes are unchanged.

items.title: Pages
items.text:
frontend/frontend/__init__.py:

from patera.desktop.ui import Application, Controller, PageContext, View, page, path


@path("/notes")
class Notes(Controller):
    @page("/<int:note_id>")
    async def detail(self, ctx: PageContext, note_id: int) -> View:
        note = await ctx.api.get_json(f"/api/notes/{note_id}")
        return View("templates/note.html", note=note, title=note["title"])


app = Application(controllers=[Notes])
  • Templates use Jinja2 with auto-escaping and strict undefined values; inheritance, includes, macros, loops, filters and globals are supported. Use View(markup=html("<h1>{{ title }}</h1>", title=value)) for inline markup, and trusted_html() only for application-authored markup.
  • Interpolate into HTML text or quoted ordinary attributes, never scripts, styles, event-handler attributes or unvalidated URLs.
  • Routes support string (default), non-negative int and path converters. Trailing slashes are ignored by default.
  • app.url_for("Notes.detail", note_id=3, query={"tab": "details"}) includes the mount after startup. Several @page decorators may alias one method; the first route is used for URL generation.
  • ctx.query maps keys to lists. ctx.spawn(coroutine) tracks a task for the page and navigation cancels it; ctx.on_cleanup(callback) registers resource cleanup.
  • Controllers live for the application lifetime; page-local state belongs in the context or in components.

ExceptionHandler classes with @handles(ValueError) methods (self, ctx, error) handle page and event errors; the most specific exception type wins. Return a View for an error page, or None from an event handler to keep the current page. Unhandled failures appear in an alert and the browser console.

items.title: Components
items.text:
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from patera.desktop.ui import Component, State, event, html, tag

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from patera.desktop.ui.types import MouseEvent


@tag("note-counter")
class Counter(Component):

    def __init__(self, app, element):
        super().__init__(app, element)
        self.state = State(count=0)

    def render(self):
        return html('<button data-ui-on-click="increment">Count: '
                    '<span data-ui-text="count"></span></button>')

    @event("click")
    def increment(self, event: MouseEvent) -> None:
        self.state["count"] += 1

Register with Application(..., components=[Counter]) and use <note-counter></note-counter> in a view. mounted() and unmounted() may be async. Assign to state to notify subscribers; in-place mutation of nested values does not notify. The newer reactive API (react, data-bind, @click) is described in the runtime guide.

items.title: Folder discovery
items.text:
Use app = Application(__name__) in your frontend package's __init__.py. The application recursively imports public modules under controllers/, components/, pages/, layouts/ and exceptions/ (or exception_handlers/). Give each folder an __init__.py.

frontend/
  __init__.py              # app = Application(__name__)
  controllers/
    __init__.py
    pages.py               # @path class Pages(Controller), @page methods
  components/
    __init__.py
    counter.py             # @tag("note-counter") class Counter(Component)
  exceptions/
    __init__.py
    errors.py              # class Errors(ExceptionHandler), @handles methods

Concrete subclasses defined in those modules are registered automatically; imported or re-exported classes are ignored, abstract classes skipped, and import errors surfaced. Explicit controllers=, components=, pages=, layouts= and exception_handlers= lists may supplement discovery.

items.title: Offline runtime and builds
items.text:
Provision a complete, pinned PyScript/Pyodide offline distribution in ui-runtime, following the official offline guide. Include PyScript's supporting modules, the interpreter's .mjs, .js and .wasm files, python_stdlib.zip, pyodide-lock.json and the packages the runtime requires, preserving its layout and licenses. Nothing downloads at application startup.

Record the actual entry paths and versions, then build and run:

patera cli ui:lock-runtime pyscript/core.js pyscript/pyodide/pyodide.mjs 2026.2.1 0.28.0.dev0 3.13
patera cli ui:build
patera cli desktop:run

The tested PyScript 2026.2.1 offline archive uses these entry paths, with Pyodide 0.28.0.dev0 and Python 3.13; extract its offline/ contents into ui-runtime/.

  • Commit runtime.json or keep it with your build inputs. Every build checks the recorded SHA-256 hashes and validates Python syntax against the recorded browser Python version.
  • The browser archive contains minimal patera / patera.desktop parent packages, portable UI modules and only allowlisted frontend files. It never installs the native Patera wheel in Pyodide.
  • The builder excludes hidden files, caches, logs, databases, bytecode and unknown file extensions. Frontend Python, HTML, JS, CSS, fonts and images are public: keep secrets out of the source root.
  • Builds are content-addressed and switch current.json atomically.
Command Purpose ui:build build once ui:watch rebuild on changes (in another terminal) ui:run build, watch in a background thread and run the desktop window ui:run prod build and launch without watching

Development windows (DEBUG=True) poll the build version and reload after a successful build; failed builds keep the working version. Frozen applications never poll or rebuild.

Use app.config for PUBLIC settings and app.asset_url("styles.css") for bundled resources. Build with the deployment's URL_PREFIX.

items.title: Desktop packaging
items.text: New desktop:spec files include UI asset preparation; both desktop:package and direct pyinstaller desktop.spec builds prepare the UI. Existing specs need the DESKTOP_ASSETS setting and the prepare_desktop_assets call from a newly generated spec; the package command rejects old specs when the UI extension is registered. Frozen applications read the artifacts from PyInstaller's resource directory and never compile sources.

items.title: Local API boundary
items.text:
Protected API prefixes require X-Patera-UI-Token on every HTTP method. The built-in API client adds it, checks status codes (APIError) and aborts fetches when cancelled. Shell and API requests require a loopback Host and reject foreign Origin and cross-site fetch metadata.

Warning

This is a browser cross-origin boundary, not authentication against other local processes. Backend authorization is still required where applicable. WebSocket routes and native bridges are not protected by this middleware. Do not enable permissive CORS for these routes.

items.title: Browser type library
items.text:
The package includes browser API stubs under patera.desktop.ui.types (DOM elements, events, networking, storage, canvas, media and common JavaScript built-ins) for static analysis:

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from patera.desktop.ui.types import MouseEvent


def clicked(event: MouseEvent) -> None:
    event.preventDefault()

Actual browser objects still come from js or pyscript.

A complete example lives in examples/desktop_ui_notes.

items.title: Desktop UI runtime
items.text: All runtime imports below come from patera.desktop.ui. Browser modules run in Pyodide; native Patera services remain behind the local HTTP API. Jinja2 is used in both interpreters. Frontend templates are application code, not a sandbox for untrusted template authors.

items.title: Pages and layouts
items.text:
from patera.desktop.ui import Application, Component, SubLayout, layout, page, tag, template


@layout
@tag("main-layout")
class MainLayout(Component):
    def markup(self):
        return template('<header>My application</header><main id="page"></main>')


@page("/notes/<int:note_id>", title="Note")
@tag("note-page")
class NotePage(Component):
    def markup(self):
        return template('<h1>Note {{ params.note_id }}</h1>')


app = Application(__name__, base_layout=MainLayout)

Every component needs a unique @tag. Classes referenced by page layout metadata are registered automatically.

@page accepts name, title, layout, sublayouts, target and extras. A title may be a sync or async callable receiving the initialized page instance. For nested layouts use sublayouts=[SubLayout(DetailLayout, target="#page")] and target="#detail-content" on the page. Each target is selected inside its owning layout. The default page target is #page, configurable with Application(default_target=...).

Navigation reuses the common prefix of the layout chain, keeping its state and DOM. Pages and removed layouts are disposed. Layout params.* and query.* fragments update when route values change; use component.context when a retained layout needs the current page context.

Controller pages remain supported and can use layouts:

from patera.desktop.ui import Controller, PageContext, View, page, path


@path("/notes")
class Notes(Controller):
    @page("/<int:note_id>", layout=MainLayout)
    async def detail(self, ctx: PageContext, note_id: int) -> View:
        note = await ctx.api.get_json(f"/api/notes/{note_id}")
        return View("templates/note.html", note=note)

items.title: Routing
items.text:
• Routes support literal segments, <name>, <str:name> / <string:name>, <int:name> and <path:name>. More specific routes win.
  • base_url can include parameters, for example Application(base_url="/<str:language>").
  • app.url_for("NotePage", note_id=3) generates a URL; base parameters must also be supplied where required.
  • await app.navigate(url, history="push") navigates; history can also be replace or none. app.router.redirect(...) supports use_base_url and base_parameters.
  • Same-origin application links are intercepted unless they have router-ignore or the UI ignore attribute. Back/Forward restores saved scroll positions. Superseded navigations cannot commit stale pages or error pages.

items.title: Jinja2 and reactive fragments
items.text:
template(source, **context) returns a deferred inline template; Template(name="templates/note.html", context={...}) loads a named template; html(source, **context) renders immediately. Templates use auto-escaping and strict undefined values, and support inheritance, includes, macros, loops and custom Application(filters={...}, globals={...}). Only .html files are registered as named templates.

Component template variables are component, app, data, query, params, args and ctx. Component properties are accessed explicitly as component.property. trusted_html() bypasses escaping; use it only for HTML you trust. Server-rendered HTML is inserted directly and never interpreted again as a frontend template.

from patera.desktop.ui import Component, react, tag, template


@tag("note-counter")
class Counter(Component):
    count = react(0)

    def markup(self):
        return template('''
          <button @click="increment">Increment</button>
          <span data-bind="count">{{ component.count }}</span>
        ''')

    def increment(self, event):
        self.count += 1
  • Assigning a reactive property re-renders the contents of matching data-bind elements; the outer element stays in place. Explicit {% bind "count" %}...{% endbind %} blocks work where a wrapper is unsuitable.
  • Bindings keep Jinja loop locals, support nesting and discard stale child bindings. Replaced descendant components are disposed and new ones initialized.
  • Use await self.rerender() when attributes or the whole component must change.
  • Mutable defaults are copied per instance; react_factory(list) accepts a factory. In-place mutations need self.invalidate("binding") or assignment of a new value.

items.title: Application data and query parameters
items.text:
• app.set_data("notes", notes) notifies data-bind="app.notes" fragments. @tag(..., data_field="notes") requests a full component re-render when that field changes.
  • query_param("filter", default="") exposes a URL query value as a descriptor. Assigning it updates browser history and query.filter bindings.
  • app.update_query_parameters({...}, history="replace") updates several values; None removes a key. app.query_parameters contains the last value per key; PageContext.query preserves lists of repeated values.

The earlier State, data-ui-text and data-ui-value APIs remain available.

items.title: Events, arguments and DOM access
items.text:
Use @click="method", @input="method" or jolt-click="method" on elements. The compatibility syntax data-ui-on-click="method" requires a matching @event("click") decorator. Methods receive the original browser event proxy.

Submit events are prevented synchronously. Add data-ui-prevent-default or data-ui-stop-propagation for other events; calling preventDefault() after an await is too late.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, cast

from patera.desktop.ui import select

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from patera.desktop.ui.types import HTMLInputElement, InputEvent

# Inside a Component:
title_input = select('input[name="title"]', required=True)

def changed(self, event: InputEvent) -> None:
    value = cast("HTMLInputElement", event.target).value
  • Use :name='JSON', data-jolt-name or data-ui-arg-name attributes to pass component arguments through self.args. Non-JSON strings stay strings.
  • select() / select_all() respect component ownership: a child host belongs to its parent, a child's interior belongs to the child. Selector shorthand [:name] works with colon attributes.
  • insert_html, hydrate and fetch_html integrate dynamically inserted markup with event binding and child initialization. Listener proxies are released on replacement.

items.title: Lifecycle and cancellation
items.text:
Decorate sync or async methods with @lifecycle(Lifecycle.BEFORE_INIT) and the other phases: EXTENSION_INIT, BEFORE_INIT_RESOLVE, AFTER_INIT, BEFORE_RERENDER, AFTER_RERENDER, AFTER_DISCONNECT. Inherited hooks execute base first; overriding a method suppresses its inherited registration.

Initialization loads dependencies, runs before-init hooks, renders, waits for child initialization, runs before-init-resolve hooks, and resolves init_complete before after-init hooks. The mounted / unmounted hooks are kept. Initialization failures reject with ElementInitializationError, keeping the original error as __cause__.

  • self.spawn(coroutine) and self.on_cleanup(callback) bind work and resources to the component lifetime; ctx.spawn / ctx.on_cleanup have the page lifetime.
  • self.api cancels outstanding requests when the component disconnects.
  • ElementDisconnectedError is cancellation, not an application failure.
  • dependencies = [OtherComponent, lazy("frontend.widgets.editor")] registers component dependencies and defers imports. This defers execution, not downloading: the offline archive contains the source.

items.title: Reactive update scheduling
items.text:
Existing applications keep synchronous binding updates. Opt into frame batching when constructing the application:

app = Application(__name__, batch_updates=True, diagnostics=True)

# Inside an async component handler:
self.count += 1                 # Python reads see the new value immediately
self.count += 1
await self.flush()              # or await app.flush()

With batching, repeated invalidations of a binding are combined and commits run on the next animation frame; flush() commits immediately, also when the window is hidden. Updates caused during rendering are handled in later batches, with a 100-batch limit to surface update loops.

flush() is a DOM commit barrier for queued bindings, not a paint, network or event-task barrier. After inserting components through a binding, use await self.wait_children() if their initialization must finish before continuing.

items.title: Diagnostics
items.text: With diagnostics=True, app.diagnostics_snapshot() returns aggregate counts and timings in milliseconds (template evaluation, DOM replacement, hydration, listeners, initialization and cleanup) and counts of components, tasks, listeners, subscriptions, fragments and queued components. app.diagnostics.reset() resets measurements. Nested measurements overlap and must not be summed.

items.title: Keyed lists
items.text:
Use a Jinja keyed block where a data-bind loop would otherwise replace every row:

<ul>
  {% keyed "items" %}
    {% for item in component.items %}
      <li data-ui-key="{{ item.id }}">
        <input value="{{ item.title }}">
        <button @click="remove" :item="{{ item.id }}">Remove</button>
      </li>
    {% endfor %}
  {% endkeyed %}
</ul>
  • Every direct row needs a stable, unique, non-empty data-ui-key. Avoid array positions when items can move. Missing or duplicate keys fail before DOM reconciliation.
  • Matching keys and element types keep their row nodes: changed text and declared attributes are patched, rows are created, removed and moved without remounting child components. Input edits, focus and selection survive.
  • Use balanced HTML; for table rows put the block inside a <tbody>.
  • Place a nested keyed or virtual list in a child component. Keyed rendering still evaluates the whole loop; it reduces DOM and lifecycle churn, not template evaluation.

items.title: Fixed-height virtual lists
items.text:
For a large sequence, a virtual block evaluates and mounts only a visible window plus overscan:

{% virtual "items", component.items, key="id", row_height=40, height=400, overscan=3 %}
  <span>{{ item.title }}</span>
  <button @click="open" :item="{{ item.id }}">Open</button>
{% endvirtual %}
  • key is a mapping key, attribute name or callable. Keys must be unique non-empty strings or integers (integer 1 and string "1" collide).
  • row_height and height are positive pixel sizes; overscan is a non-negative integer. Defaults are 40, 400 and 3. Variable-height rows are not supported.
  • Use a normal block container, not a table or select element.
  • Off-screen rows are disposed, so keep persistent edits and selection in application state.

items.title: Errors, authorization and application events
items.text:
ExceptionHandler methods decorated with @handles(ErrorType) receive (ctx, error). Dispatch checks the exception's MRO, then compatible registered types, then its cause chain. Methods may return a View or call await app.show_error_page(ErrorComponent, error=error, args={...}). Error pages do not change the current URL.

Use @auth() or @auth(roles=["editor"]) on page and layout classes or controller handlers. Override Application.is_authenticated() and check_user_roles(roles) (sync or async). All applicable layout and page requirements are checked before mounting; failures raise AuthenticationError or AuthorizationError.

Warning

These hooks control the UI only. Enforce permissions on the backend as well.

app.on(name, callback) returns an unsubscribe function; await app.emit(name, *args) awaits subscribers. Built-in route-start and route-finished events receive the page context.

items.title: Cached and server-rendered components
items.text:
@tag(..., cache=True, cache_duration=30) caches the markup provider's result for 30 seconds. The key includes tag, group, route and query parameters and args. Concurrent requests share one load. Application(templates_cache_duration=..., templates_cache_cleanup_interval=...) sets defaults; clear_templates_cache() and clean_templates_cache() invalidate entries.

For native rendering, configure the backend explicitly:

DESKTOP_UI = DesktopUIConfig(
    SERVER_COMPONENTS_PATH="/api/ui-components",
    SERVER_COMPONENTS={"default/server-card": "components/card.html"},
)

Then declare @tag("server-card", use_server=True) on a frontend component. The endpoint must be inside API_PATHS, so the UI session-token guard applies. Only allowlisted group/tag pairs select templates, which receive the request values as args, query and params. DesktopUI.register_server_component(tag, template, group="default", context=callback) adds server context; the callback receives (request, payload). Never choose a template path from request input.

app.fetch_html and app.prefetch_html use the same rendering and cache path. The API client supports JSON and text responses, CRUD helpers and cancellation, and distinguishes APIError, NetworkError and JsonResponseError.

items.title: Compatibility boundaries
items.text: This is a Python counterpart of JoltUI, not a TypeScript execution layer. Jinja expressions refer to Python values; there is no doT engine or JavaScript template evaluation. The packaged browser runtime targets PyScript/Pyodide on the main thread, not MicroPython or workers. The extension registers no routes and adds no dependencies to applications that do not use it.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
This section takes you from an empty folder to a running Patera application.

  1. Installation: install Patera and the optional extras you need.
  2. Quick start: write a configuration, an application class and a controller.
  3. Project layout: how Patera finds controllers, middleware and other components in your package.
  4. Running the application: the development and production servers and the patera command.

When the basics are in place, continue with the Guide.

Complete example

A small, complete application lives in examples/basic_app in the Patera repository.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Patera requires Python 3.13 or newer. We recommend uv.

uvpip 
uv init --python 3.13 my-app
cd my-app
uv add "patera[dev]"     # core + uvicorn/watchfiles for the development server

pip install "patera[dev]"

items.title: Extras
items.text:
Optional features are installed with extras:

Extra Installs Purpose prod granian production server (patera prod) dev uvicorn, watchfiles, websockets development server with auto-reload (patera dev) testing pytest, pytest-asyncio, httpx, ... testing tools (patera test) database patera-database async SQLAlchemy integration migrate patera-migrate SQL migrations (pyway) auth patera-auth authentication/authorization middleware caching patera-caching response caching (in-memory) caching-redis / caching-sqlite + redis / aiosqlite Redis or SQLite cache backends taskmanager patera-taskmanager scheduled and background tasks (APScheduler) email patera-email SMTP e-mail client apiinterface patera-apiinterface declarative clients for external HTTP APIs joltui patera-joltui JoltUI server components with typed group registration admin patera-admin admin dashboard aiinterface patera-aiinterface LLM chat interface (experimental) desktop patera-desktop desktop windows and packaging (experimental) desktop-ui patera-desktop-ui Python browser UI for desktop apps (experimental) all the server extensions admin, API interface, authentication, caching, SQL, migrations, e-mail, task manager and JoltUI 
uv add "patera[database,auth,caching]"

What patera[all] contains

patera[all] is the server-extension bundle. It does not install the experimental AI or desktop packages, optional cache backends, or every optional provider.
