  • patera-admin: an unknown database or model on a record page answers 404, and an unknown e-mail sender 400, instead of 500.
  • patera-taskmanager: a persistent job store (SQLAlchemyJobStore, ...) made startup fail, because jobs were stored as bound methods. Methods of the task manager are now stored by name (run_scheduled_job); job_callable(job) returns the method a job runs.
  • Core: the missing-configuration error names the @app(...) decorator.
  • Core: database sessions opened in a WebSocket handler are closed when it returns.
  • patera-database: session_scope() (and work_session() outside @transactional) inside a request keeps the request's user and request object, leaves the request's sessions alone, and closes other databases' sessions opened in the block (they leaked).
  • patera-auth: @login_required and @role_required keep a custom exception class in either stacking order.
  • patera-taskmanager: jobs declared with @schedule_job are added again when the application's lifespan runs again.
  • Core: an environment variable for one field of a nested setting (PATERA_ASSISTANT__API_KEY) keeps the other fields of the class default instead of failing them as missing.
  • Core: invalid UTF-8 in a form body answers 400 instead of failing; malformed cookies are skipped; a file that shrinks while being sent ends the response properly; CORS headers on routing errors; consistent {"status", "message", "data"} error bodies; run_sync_or_async() awaits async callable objects and functools.partial objects instead of running them in a thread.
  • patera-admin: missing task manager translations; sorting by level follows severity and line numbers sort numerically; unknown sort columns fall back to newest first.
  • patera-auth: passwords longer than 72 bytes no longer raise, and a malformed stored hash no longer crashes the check.
  • patera-caching: the memory backend honours per-entry durations longer than its default; SQLite clear() treats _ and % in the prefix literally; Redis clear() refuses to run without a prefix.
  • patera-database: @query INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements no longer crash.
  • patera-database: removed DeclarativeBaseModel.db_configs_name(), which always raised AttributeError.
  • patera-database: disconnect() forgets the session factory, so a later session reconnects instead of opening connections on the disposed engine that were never closed.
  • patera-migrate: per-database command prefixes; percent-encoded credentials in the URI are decoded.
  • Core: patera test accepts pytest options in any order (patera test -k login -q failed with "unrecognized arguments"), and a missing environment file is a one-line error instead of a traceback.
  • Core: when auto-discovery finds no application because a module failed to import, the error names that module instead of asking for an import string.
  • Core: routes joined from @path("/") and @get("/hello") are stored as /hello, not //hello.
  • patera-migrate: MIGRATE_SQL_MIGRATION_PREFIX, _SEPARATOR and _SUFFIXES now take effect (they were ignored); files in the migration folder with another ending are skipped, and a misnamed migration is an error. pyway is limited to <0.4.
  • patera-taskmanager: the scheduler is the single source of truth for job state; APScheduler is limited to version 3 (<4), since version 4 changes its API.

items.title: Experimental packages
items.text:
patera-aiinterface and patera-desktop are marked Alpha.

patera-aiinterface 0.11.0: - The embedding libraries moved to the augmentation extra (pip install "patera-aiinterface[augmentation]") and are imported only when an augmentation provider starts; the unused openai and docstring-parser dependencies are gone. - One vector column type: pgvector's (augmentation_provider.embeddings.VectorColumn); the package's own database_types.Vector was removed. - Removed the unused STREAM and TOOL_CHOICE settings and the @tool decorator. RESPONSE_FORMAT now defaults to plain text and is sent when set; ORGANIZATION_ID, PROJECT_ID and MAX_RETRIES are used; TEMPERATURE=None leaves the provider's default. - The history stores the user's message without the augmentation texts, and nothing is saved when the call fails. - AUGMENTATION settings default when not configured; the embedding model cache no longer changes process-wide environment variables. - The chat pipeline lives in AiService: current system prompt, then the session's history, then the user message (with augmentation texts when used). Service providers only send messages: BaseServiceProvider.complete(messages, configs) and stream(messages, configs). - @history methods take an explicit session_id argument (None starts a new session, returned in ChatResponse.session_id); the route-based @session_id decorator was removed. - BaseHistoryProvider is a small interface (load, append, new_session_id), and SqlHistoryProvider stores messages in its own transaction, so history works outside requests and needs no commit by the handler. - The system prompt is no longer stored in the history; the current one is always sent. - HISTORY_LIMIT (default 10) caps how many earlier messages are sent. - HISTORY_SUMMARY (HistorySummaryConfig): a rolling summary of older messages is sent instead of them and updated in the background (one extra call every EVERY messages). It is stored as a role="summary" row of the messages table; SqlHistoryProvider supports it out of the box. - Streaming methods are iterated directly: async for chunk in service.method(...). - Retrieved documents go in a context message before the user message (CONTEXT_TEMPLATE) instead of being pasted under the question. - On PostgreSQL the document search is one pgvector query (closest documents by cosine distance); other databases compare the candidates in Python (RETRIEVAL: auto, database or python). base_query() limits the candidates; add_documents() / add_document() embed and store texts; embed(), search() and relevant_texts() are public. - REWRITE_QUERY: with history, the model first rewrites a follow-up question into a standalone one for the search (REWRITE_PROMPT). - ChatMessage has only role and content (the unused thinking, name and tool_call_id fields and the "tool" role are gone). Ollama reports finish_reason="length" for an answer cut off at the token limit; OpenAI answers fill request_id, and created_at is ISO 8601 text for both providers. - augmentation_provider.embeddings keeps only VectorColumn; its Python distance helpers were removed. - Methods without @history work outside a request, and a missing history or augmentation provider fails at startup. - In a @transactional handler the SQL history and the documents use the request's session (no "database is locked" on SQLite; they commit or roll back with the request). A streamed answer, saved after the request's transaction has ended, uses a transaction of its own. - Concurrent writes to one chat session (two quick messages, or two summary updates) no longer get the same position or a second summary row, also across worker processes and inside @transactional requests that commit later: each write first locks the chat session until it commits, with an advisory lock on PostgreSQL and the database's write lock on SQLite. That lock is taken before the in-process one, so a write waiting for another request's commit no longer deadlocks that request's next write (on PostgreSQL it waited forever). Other databases take turns within a process. - <:name> placeholders are filled in one pass: text inserted by an argument, such as a user's message, can no longer pull other arguments into the prompt. - The embedding model is loaded on first use, in a worker thread, instead of when the application starts (CLI commands no longer load it); load_embedding_model() can be overridden. - Document search decides between pgvector and Python from the database URI, so it works before the database has connected (it failed with "Engine not initialized", e.g. in CLI commands).

patera-desktop: rewritten, with only one feature for now. The Desktop extension adds the CLI command desktop:run [dev|prod]: it starts the application in a separate process, as patera dev or patera prod would (on 127.0.0.1 and the PORT setting), shows DESKTOP.INDEX_PAGE (default /) in a pywebview window, and stops the application when the window is closed. The launcher, the frontend bridge, frontend tools and the PATERA_DESKTOP_* settings are gone, and so is the core command patera desktop. python -m patera.cli now runs the patera command. desktop:package [folder] packages the application as a program with PyInstaller (extra patera-desktop[pyinstaller]), by default into dist/desktop/<APP_NAME>/: the program runs the server in a background thread with run_in_window(App), on a free port, and writes its log files to user_data_dir(APP_NAME). Before the application starts, run_in_window loads the installation's settings file, settings_file(APP_NAME) (settings.env in that folder), like .env during development. The package ships a PyInstaller hook so the patera.* extensions are found also in editable (workspace) installs. Window settings in DESKTOP: TITLE, WIDTH/HEIGHT (1024 × 720), MIN_WIDTH/MIN_HEIGHT, REMEMBER_GEOMETRY (size, position and maximized state restored at the next start, on by default), MAXIMIZED, FULLSCREEN, RESIZABLE, ON_TOP, CONFIRM_CLOSE, BACKGROUND_COLOR, TEXT_SELECT (on), ZOOMABLE, PERSIST_STORAGE (cookies and local storage kept in the user's data folder, on by default; pywebview forgets them at every close otherwise), ICON (also the spec file's default icon), DEV_TOOLS and GUI. desktop:env writes desktop.env, the packaged program's settings: every setting the configuration declares, defaults commented out, required ones empty. desktop:package bundles it, refuses to build while a required setting is empty, and warns about values that look like secrets. The program loads environment variables, then the installation's settings.env, then desktop.env; ${PATERA_DATA_DIR} is the user's data folder. desktop:run loads desktop.env under the development .env. A configuration that declares SECRET_KEY gets a key per installation, made at the first start and kept in settings.env. A packaged program reuses the port of its last start, so the page's origin and local storage stay the same. user_data_dir also knows iOS (Application Support in the app's sandbox) and Android (the app's internal storage, $HOME). desktop:spec [path] writes a PyInstaller spec file (default desktop.spec) with the defaults as settings to edit (hidden imports, data files, icon, console, one file, own entry script). The application package is copied without what running and developing it leave there (__pycache__, log files, SQLite databases, .env, tool caches; PACKAGE_EXCLUDES in the spec file). desktop:package [folder] [spec] builds with the spec file when it exists, otherwise with a generated one in build/desktop/. patera-desktop now depends on uvicorn.

items.title: Repository layout
items.text:
The repository is a uv workspace:

Path Content src/patera the core package packages/patera-* the extension packages, all in the patera namespace examples/ example applications tests/ unit, integration and extension tests docs/ this documentation (Zensical) scripts/ version bump, build and publish helpers

items.title: Development environment
items.text:
uv sync --all-packages --all-extras    # note: the AI interface pulls in PyTorch
uv run pytest                          # tests/ (unit, integration and extension tests)
PATERA_TEST_PG_URI=postgresql+asyncpg://... uv run pytest   # also run the pgvector tests
uv run pytest --cov
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy src/patera packages --follow-imports=silent

CI runs the tests, Ruff, mypy, a browser-bootstrap syntax check (python scripts/check_browser.py) and the packaging checks on Windows, Linux and macOS with Python 3.13 and 3.14.

items.title: Pull requests
items.text:
• Changes to public behaviour come with tests and a documentation update in docs/.
  • New public names follow the public API conventions.
  • Add an entry to CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased; list breaking changes first.

items.title: Releasing
items.text: The scripts in scripts/ share one release.py helper and run from any directory.

items.title: Version bumps
items.text:
Linux/macOSWindows 
./scripts/bump_version.sh patch --dry-run
./scripts/bump_version.sh patch
./scripts/bump_version.sh minor --update-dependency-floors

.\scripts\bump_version.ps1 patch -DryRun
.\scripts\bump_version.ps1 patch
.\scripts\bump_version.ps1 minor -UpdateDependencyFloors

Each package increments its own version. To set every release package to a coordinated candidate, use --version 1.0.0rc1 --update-dependency-floors --dry-run (PowerShell: -Version 1.0.0rc1 -UpdateDependencyFloors -DryRun), then 1.0.0rc2 and finally 1.0.0. Failures restore the original package metadata and lockfile. Dependency minimums stay unchanged unless the floor option is given.

items.title: Build and publish
items.text:
./scripts/build_all.sh --dry-run      # preview the order
./scripts/build_all.sh                # wheel/sdist pairs, verified, twine check --strict
python scripts/smoke_wheels.py        # install all wheels together and check imports
./scripts/publish_all.sh --dry-run    # preflight without credentials
./scripts/publish_all.sh

Builds replace dist/ only when every package passes, and release.json records SHA-256 hashes. Publishing needs UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN (or UV_PUBLISH_USERNAME and UV_PUBLISH_PASSWORD) from the environment or .env.pypi; never commit credentials. Uploads run in dependency order and stop on failure.

items.title: Release checklist
items.text:
1. Bump versions, review compatibility and the lockfile.
  2. Update CHANGELOG.md.
  3. Run tests, lint/type checks, and UI browser/frozen checks as applicable.
  4. Build distributions and inspect contents when resources change.
  5. Run the publish dry-run, then publish.
  6. Tag the release (git tag v<core-version>) and push the tag.
  7. Publish the documentation for the new version (see Writing the documentation).

items.title: Writing the documentation
items.text: The documentation is built with Zensical from the Markdown files in docs/ and the configuration in zensical.toml at the repository root. The Python API pages are generated from the source code with mkdocstrings, and versions are published with Zensical's fork of mike.

items.title: Preview and build
items.text:
Run from the repository root:

uvx --with mkdocstrings-python zensical serve           # http://localhost:8000, live reload
uvx --with mkdocstrings-python zensical build --clean   # static site in site/

site/ is build output; keep it out of version control.

items.title: Structure
items.text:
Folder Content Style getting-started/ installation and a first application step by step, for newcomers guide/ one page per core feature explains concepts with examples extensions/ one page per extension package setup, settings, usage deployment.md running in production checklist reference/ configuration options, CLI, public API, Python API complete, terse look-up project/ changelog, versioning, contributing, these notes

Add a new page to the nav in zensical.toml, or it will not appear in the navigation.

  • The changelog and license pages include CHANGELOG.md and LICENSE from the repository root with snippets (--8<-- "CHANGELOG.md"); edit the originals.
  • The Python API pages use patera.module blocks. Docstrings use the Sphinx style (:param name:). A new public module needs a page under reference/api/.
  • Keep examples runnable and consistent with the examples/ applications.
  • Changes to public behaviour should update the documentation in the same pull request.

items.title: Publishing versions
items.text:
Each documentation version is a separate build, stored on the gh-pages branch by mike. The version selector in the header lists them (project.extra.version in zensical.toml).

Install the Zensical fork of mike (it reads zensical.toml and runs zensical build):

uv tool install "mike @ git+https://github.com/squidfunk/mike.git" \
    --with mkdocstrings-python --with-executables-from zensical

Deploy a release from its Git tag, so the generated API reference matches the released code:

git checkout v0.123.0
mike deploy --push --update-aliases 0.123 latest   # first time: also run the next line
mike set-default --push latest

The development documentation of main:

git checkout main
mike deploy --push dev

Useful commands:

Command Purpose mike list show deployed versions and aliases mike serve preview the versioned site from gh-pages locally mike delete --push 0.120 remove a version mike retitle --push 0.123 "0.123 (beta)" change the title in the selector

Versions are created per minor release (0.123, 1.0); a patch release redeploys its minor version. See Versioning.

Transitional tooling

Zensical's mike fork is transitional until Zensical ships native versioning. Commands and the gh-pages layout stay compatible with mike 2.x.

items.title: GitHub Actions
items.text:
Publish the documentation automatically when a release tag is pushed, and the dev version on every push to main. Enable GitHub Pages for the gh-pages branch in the repository settings.

# .github/workflows/docs.yml
name: Documentation
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - run: >
          uv tool install "mike @ git+https://github.com/squidfunk/mike.git"
          --with mkdocstrings-python --with-executables-from zensical
      - run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
      - name: Deploy dev
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: mike deploy --push dev
      - name: Deploy release
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        run: |
          VERSION=$(echo "${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" | cut -d. -f1,2)
          mike deploy --push --update-aliases "$VERSION" latest
          mike set-default --push latest

items.title: Package versions
items.text:
Patera and its extension packages follow semantic versioning: major.minor.patch.

  • Before 1.0, a minor release may contain breaking changes. They are listed first in each release of the changelog.
  • Each extension package has its own version, independent of the core. Every package declares the core versions it supports (currently patera>=0.121).
  • A core 1.0 release does not change every extension's maturity: the AI interface, desktop and desktop UI packages stay experimental until their own stability requirements are met.

Pin versions in applications and read the changelog before upgrading a minor version.

items.title: Documentation versions
items.text:
The documentation is versioned per minor release of the core package (0.123, 0.124, 1.0, ...). Patch releases update the documentation of their minor version.

Version Content latest (alias, default) the newest stable release X.Y the documentation as it was released with that version dev the main branch, for the next unreleased version

Use the version selector in the header to switch. Pages of older versions stay available, so the documentation matches the version you have installed.

How versions are published is described in Writing the documentation.

items.title: Reference
items.text:
Look-up material for everyday use.

  • Configuration options: every built-in setting with its default.
  • CLI commands: the patera command and the commands extensions add.
  • Public API conventions: packages, imports, entry points and naming rules.

items.title: Python API
items.text:
Generated from the source code and its docstrings with mkdocstrings:

  • patera: the application, configuration, request, response and helpers.

items.title: The patera command
items.text:
Command Description patera dev [--app app:App] [--env-file .env] Development server (Uvicorn) with auto-reload. Loads .env, .env.dev or .env.local if no file is given. patera prod [--app app:App] [--env-file .env.prod] Production server (Granian, prod extra). DEBUG is forced off; only an explicit --env-file is loaded. patera cli [--app app:App] [--env-file FILE] Controller:command [args...] Runs an application CLI command. patera cli --list Lists application commands and their help. patera test [--env-file FILE] [pytest args...] Runs pytest after loading .env.test (or the given file). Everything after -- goes to pytest unchanged. patera agents [codex\|claude\|all] [--dry-run] [--force] Generates coding-agent instructions.

See Running the application for environment files and address resolution.

items.title: Packages and imports
items.text:
Distribution names use kebab case (patera-taskmanager); imports live under the patera namespace (patera.taskmanager). Class names describe their role, so the AI distribution exports AiService. Existing public names remain supported.

Distribution Import Entry point Configuration patera patera Patera BaseConfig patera-admin patera.admin AdminInterface AdminConfig patera-aiinterface patera.aiinterface AiService AiServiceConfig patera-apiinterface patera.apiinterface ApiInterface class/method decorators patera-auth patera.auth Authentication AuthConfig patera-caching patera.caching Caching CachingConfig patera-database patera.database.sql SqlDatabase SqlDatabaseConfig patera-desktop patera.desktop Desktop DesktopConfig patera-desktop-ui patera.desktop.ui DesktopUI DesktopUIConfig patera-email patera.email EmailClient EmailConfig patera-joltui patera.joltui PateraJoltui JoltuiConfig patera-migrate patera.migrate Migrate MigrateConfig patera-taskmanager patera.taskmanager TaskManager TaskManagerConfig

SQL classes intentionally live under patera.database.sql, leaving room for other database implementations.

items.title: Naming rules
items.text:
• PascalCase for new classes, treating acronyms as words (Api, Ai, Sql).
  • snake_case for methods, decorators and model fields.
  • UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for configuration settings.
  • New configuration classes use the component's full class name followed by Config; the established shorter names above remain canonical.
  • Existing names such as DesktopUI remain compatibility exceptions.

JoltUI is written JoltUI in prose, joltui in distribution and import names, and Joltui in Python classes. PateraJoltui keeps its integration name; JoltuiGroupHandler and JoltuiRequest describe protocol-facing roles.

items.title: Installation bundle
items.text: patera[all] means the server-extension bundle: admin, API interface, authentication, caching, SQL, migrations, e-mail, task manager and JoltUI. It does not install the experimental AI or desktop packages, optional cache backends, or every optional provider.

items.title: Maturity
items.text: A core 1.0 release does not automatically change every extension's maturity. The AI interface, desktop and desktop UI packages remain experimental until their own stability requirements are met.
